meta.subtitle: What the system is, what it guarantees, and what this document does not cover

sections.title: What this system is
sections.summary: The shape of the platform and who it serves.
sections.narrative:
The Shop platform sells physical products to customers and gives ops staff a back-office for the catalogue and refunds [[shop.purpose]]. Two frontends talk to a single backend-for-frontend, which fans out to the domain APIs behind it.

Ownership follows the deploy boundary: the web team owns the two frontends, the platform team owns the BFF and everything behind it [[shop.ownership]]. A frontend release therefore never requires a backend release.

The elements below are derived from the container diagram, so this list cannot drift from it.

sections.title: Trust boundaries
sections.summary: What runs where, and what each side is allowed to assume about the other.
sections.narrative:
There is exactly one way in. The BFF is the only container reachable from the public internet [[network.public-entry]], and nothing inside the private network accepts connections from outside it [[network.private-isolated]].

Authentication lives entirely at that edge. The BFF issues and validates browser sessions [[bff.session-owner]] and forwards a verified user id inward on every request [[bff.forwards-identity]]. The domain APIs behind it trust that header and never issue or verify tokens themselves [[bff.no-token-issue]].

> Two consequences worth holding onto: a domain API reached by any route other than the BFF has
> no authentication at all, and a session bug is a single-service bug.

sections.title: Data model
sections.summary: Tables, keys, and the rules that are enforced in the database rather than in code.
sections.narrative:
Seven tables, split between an identity group and a commerce group.

Two conventions are enforced rather than agreed. Every money column stores an integer number of cents [[money.integer-cents]], which is why totals can be summed without rounding drift. And the `orders` table has exactly one writer, the Order API [[orders.single-writer]] — the Catalogue API reads it through a view and holds no write access.

Everything below is read off the ERD spec: column counts, keys, cardinalities and delete rules.

sections.title: API surface
sections.summary: Every operation the frontends can call.
sections.narrative:
Ten operations, all reached through the BFF. The list is generated from the endpoint spec, so a route added in code and imported here shows up without anyone editing this page.

`POST /webhooks/stripe` is the exception to the one-way-in rule: Stripe calls it directly, and it authenticates the caller by signature rather than by session [[webhook.signature-auth]].
